# Scope

This checkpoint audits the source and makes minimal, deterministic coding
changes. **It does not finalize the modeling cohort, select predictors, fit
models, impute values, or create train/test splits.** All encounters remain
in the normalized audit data. No patient-level rows are displayed here.

The target is 1 for source label `<30`, and 0 for `>30` or `NO`. This is
less-than-30-day readmission as coded by the source, rather than a claim about
all readmissions across all hospitals. `NO` denotes no recorded readmission.

# Source integrity

The original UCI files are left unchanged and verified against committed
SHA-256 checksums before every audit. The archive contains two CSV files.
The mapping file contains **three separate header-delimited tables**; the
reader parses them separately and preserves quoted descriptions containing commas.

```{r provenance}
knitr::kable(verify_raw(), caption = "Original source files and SHA-256 checksums")
```

Source: [UCI dataset 296](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/296/diabetes-130-us-hospitals-for-years-1999-2008).
Dataset DOI: [10.24432/C5230J](https://doi.org/10.24432/C5230J). License: CC BY 4.0.
Background: Strack et al. (2014),
[10.1155/2014/781670](https://doi.org/10.1155/2014/781670).

# Encounters and repeated patients

```{r overview}
knitr::kable(audit$overview, caption = "Source dimensions, identifiers, and repeated encounters")
```

There are `r format(audit$overview$value[audit$overview$measure == "unique_patients"], big.mark = ",")`
distinct patients. A repeated patient is not a duplicate encounter. Retain
these encounters for now, then keep all encounters for each patient together
in the future test split and cross-validation folds. IDs remain character
strings and are tracking variables, not predictors. Encounter IDs are not
treated as validated dates or a basis for temporal validation.

# Missingness and normalization

```{r missing-table}
m <- audit$missingness
knitr::kable(m[m$normalized_missing > 0, ], digits = 2,
             caption = "Explicit missing-value codes; no imputation has been applied")
```

```{r missing-plot}
shown <- m[m$normalized_missing > 0, ]
ggplot(shown, aes(reorder(variable, missing_percent), missing_percent)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#436B83") + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Missing (%)", title = "Missingness varies substantially across fields") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

Applied rules:

- Convert the literal `?` to R `NA`.
- Convert `Unknown/Invalid` in gender to `NA`; retain these encounters.
- Preserve the literal `None` category in `A1Cresult` and `max_glu_serum`.
  It represents a test not performed, rather than an empty numeric value.
- Store the eight count/length variables as integers. Store categorical
  predictors, including admission/discharge codes and age intervals, as factors.
  Keep diagnosis codes categorical; do not coerce ICD codes to continuous numbers.
- Retain source outcome `readmitted` for audit, and add binary `early_readmission`.
  Neither outcome may appear among model predictors.

Weight is a candidate for omission because of extreme missingness. Specialty
and payer information also require a deliberate missing-data strategy. These
are recommendations for review, not implemented predictor exclusions. Any
data-dependent choice of omission/pooling thresholds, factor vocabularies,
imputation values, scaling, spline knots, or feature selection must be learned
within training folds. The full-source normalized RDS is **audit-only**, not
a model matrix; rebuild factor levels and preprocessing within each fold.

# Target coding check

```{r target}
knitr::kable(audit$outcome, digits = 2, caption = "Source outcome labels (full-data descriptive audit)")
```

Early readmission accounts for
`r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * mean(audit$normalized$early_readmission))` of source encounters.
This full-source summary checks label coding. It is not an estimate of
validation or test performance. Class balance motivates reporting sensitivity
and precision alongside overall classification error. Predictor-outcome plots
will use training data only after shared splits are fixed.

# Category mappings and quality flags

```{r flags}
knitr::kable(audit$flags, caption = "Issues and cohort-relevant flags; categories can overlap")
```

```{r unknown-codes}
u <- audit$mapping_counts
knitr::kable(u[u$unknown_description, ],
             caption = "Mapped codes with unknown/unavailable meanings, plus any unmapped codes")
```

The literal `NULL` in the mapping is a dictionary description, not an R null.
These codes stay as distinct source categories at this stage. Model-time
handling is still to be agreed. All observed admission/discharge codes are
checked against the supplied dictionary; an unrecognized code is reported
without inventing its meaning. Full mapping counts and categorical-level
counts are saved as CSVs for review.

# Proposed cohort scenarios

```{r cohort}
knitr::kable(audit$cohort_scenarios, caption = "Alternative cohorts: counts only, not applied exclusions")
```

The supplied dictionary labels codes **11, 19, 20, 21** as expired and
**13, 14** as hospice. Excluding expired discharges is appropriate to consider
for a discharge-time readmission target. Hospice exclusion is a separate
scope decision: hospice does not itself make readmission impossible.
We therefore show both scenarios and preserve every source encounter.

No records are dropped because a diagnosis, demographic field, weight, payer,
or specialty is missing. No first-encounter-only restriction is applied.
All four team members should use the same agreed cohort once finalized.

# Outputs and next decisions

Generated locally (ignored by Git):

- `results/audit/`: aggregate tables, source checksums, provenance, session
  information, and this rendered HTML.
- `data/derived/normalized_audit_only.rds`: all source encounters after the
  deterministic normalization above; identifiers and both outcome forms remain.

Before modeling, agree on the cohort, predictor set, missing-category handling,
and primary comparison metric. Then freeze shared patient-level splits and
fold assignments before outcome-focused exploration or model tuning.
